opus_only: Early track records often differ from later ones because a small manager can exploit a good anomaly or take big risks with little to lose.
Asset growth constrains capacity and almost inevitably changes the strategy, making the return process non-stationary.
Fat-tailed (Cauchy-Paretian) return processes have infinite variance, so the Sharpe ratio cannot assess them.
Merger arbitrage and similar strategies have short-option-like return distributions exposed to rare cataclysms, as LTCM showed.
The Sortino ratio still requires a stationary, well-understood distribution to be meaningful.
No single statistic should be relied on to judge risky strategies.
